However, Mifuyu Niimura, back from the memorial service, is enraged by this and slaughters everyone except Natsumi Kogori.\n　10 years later, Natsumi Kogori, apparently hospitalized somewhere from the mental shock of that time, spends every day with a gloomy expression.

Called by Mifuyu Niimura, mastermind of the Megasawa City case, Ryoji Kogori and the others agonize over whether to really kill the targets, but seeing Natsumi Kogori with Mifuyu Niimura, they hold back. Back from the memorial service, Mifuyu is enraged and tries to club Natsumi Kogori, who is in her way, to death with a hammer, but strikes Haruka Niimura, who shielded her.\n　Haruka is rushed to the hospital and is not badly hurt, but Mifuyu is left dazed by the fear of her daughter's hatred. Natsumi, Haruka and Akane Kogori apologize for driving Mifuyu this far, and the two families reconcile.\n　Ten years later, Natsumi is specially allowed to attend Eiichiro Niimura's thirteenth-year memorial service in the Arata settlement. But it is due to her danger sense, and the Kogori couple see her off uneasy about what may happen there.

Natsumi Kogori and the others, come to the Arata settlement, learn of the murders over the past ten years and of the old people's suicides that have continued for decades. Erika Niimura, the Grand Witch, says she had them come hoping to get information that might lead to a solution from Natsumi Kogori and the others, who know about what happened in Megasawa (at first she had planned to hear it from the Kogori couple).\n　But Natsumi Kogori is suddenly attacked by a group dressed as shinigami.

Kana Niimura, who lost her mother Sakura Niimura, hated the killer and was determined to judge them with her own hands. Kotaro Niimura led the residents to attack Natsumi Kogori and the others, but everyone who turned against them was killed by Kana Niimura, who had used Droga. But Kana Niimura too was deeply wounded, and passed away as Erina Goto watched over her.\n　On August 1, Kana Niimura's birthday, Erina Goto goes alone to the Arata settlement, and while holding a memorial for Kana Niimura and the others, she thinks about how the tragedy could have been prevented. But in the middle of it, a strange sound rings out from somewhere, and the settlement―

Erina Goto thinks the curse-killings may have begun with Sakura Niimura's death and with what happened in Megasawa City. If Droga was sent to Mifuyu Niimura to be tested on people, many things add up. The curse-killings also seem to arise from the residents' suspicion of one another, yet why they happen so conveniently remains a question.\n　Still, that distrust seems real: after the thirteenth-year memorial service, Natsumi Kogori and the others are attacked by armed residents, and underground by Kotaro Niimura as well. Natsumi Kogori is knocked out by Kotaro Niimura's attack, but survives thanks to the metal Grand Witch's Noh mask tucked inside her clothes. Then, in a dream, Eiichiro Niimura tells her, "You can no longer use danger sense" and "You must not pursue the truth."\n　One of Haruka Niimura's eyes is green―

The killing of Ryoji Kogori, Natsumi Kogori's father, makes Erina Goto resolve to find the culprit. She asks Haruka Niimura for help as well, and they decide to split up and gather information. On her way back from Zahha, however, she notices her bicycle has a flat tire and has no choice but to push it home. Partway there she seems to realize something important and hurries toward the police station where Natsumi Kogori is, but she is beaten to death by someone.

The killing of Ryoji Kogori, Natsumi Kogori's father, makes Erina Goto resolve to find the culprit. Thinking that Haruka Niimura may be involved in the case, she arms herself with everything she can (kitchen knives and tools) and goes to collect Natsumi Kogori from the police station. On the way they are attacked by someone in a Noh mask; Natsumi Kogori is beheaded, and Erina Goto ―

Natsumi Kogori senses who the victims of the flayed-body case are and that its culprit is Haruka Niimura, and flees into the mountains to protect her from the police. In the mountains, however, they are attacked by a monstrous figure in a Noh mask and red robes, armed with a nata and a hammer ― a shinigami ― and Haruka Niimura is left near death.\n　Erina Goto rushes to the scene with Daijiro Ise, but the shinigami is gone: only an unhurt Natsumi Kogori and a gravely injured Haruka Niimura. While Haruka Niimura is in surgery, Erina Goto seems to realize something, presses Akane Kogori when she comes to the hospital and urges her to turn herself in. Mifuyu Niimura, a candidate for culprit, is found as a burned body in a fire at her home.\n　2 years on, Natsumi Kogori, Haruka Niimura and Erina Goto visit the victims' graves.

Natsumi Kogori is shown Ryoji Kogori's body. According to Daijiro Ise, the Megasawa City murders and the flayed-body case occur to match the memorial years of the rites for Eiichiro Niimura.\n　Back home, Natsumi Kogori sets about preparing her father's rites, but on seeing the letter from Ryoji Kogori that Erina Goto found, she realizes that something dreadful is stirring behind it all. Then Haruka Niimura is carried off by the shinigami, and they meet on the roof of their apartment building. The shinigami is revealed to be Mifuyu Niimura. Natsumi Kogori apologizes over Eiichiro Niimura, but is answered with "That is not the problem," and Mifuyu Niimura throws herself from the roof together with Haruka Niimura; from then on she is missing.

The killing of Natsumi Kogori's father Ryoji Kogori makes Erina Goto resolve to find the culprit. Haruka Niimura talks her round and she promises on the surface not to investigate, but means to go on alone. Her inquiries suggest the flayed-body case arose from the Niimura-Kogori feud, and she questions Haruka Niimura. Haruka Niimura claims she cursed Ryoji Kogori to death and caused the Megasawa City murders, but far too much of that makes no sense.\n　When the Kogori come home she stays till morning, then goes to their house with Haruka Niimura to prove the curse a sham. There, however, Natsumi Kogori, Akane Kogori and Mifuyu Niimura are already dead, and Haruka Niimura kills herself to protect Erina Goto from the curse.\n　The next day, rescued from the burning Kogori house, Erina Goto despairs of her uselessness and gives up all thought.

荒田集落での事件やドローガというものは、糸姫が死月妖花によって生かされた結果生み出されたものであり、その目的は死月妖花を成長させ、皇子が眠る元木町へ行くことであった。しかし古郡なつみに諭されたことで元木町へ共に行こうと誘われる。その優しさに触れた糸姫は自分のしたことを顧みて、死月妖花そのものを滅ぼしてほしいと願う。結果、第三世代の血により死月妖花は死滅し、糸姫は「古郡なつみのそばに生まれ変わりたい」と思いながら消えていく。

On Haruka Niimura's advice, Natsumi Kogori hides at Erina Goto's house (not knowing why). Erina secretly contacts Daijiro Ise; it emerges that the Megasawa City murderer, the shinigami, is after Natsumi. The shinigami then bursts into the house, plainly inhuman, leaping abnormally and dodging bullets. Natsumi slips out and is drawn to Central Park by a strange voice.\n　There, Ryoji Kogori, who should be dead, appears as a ravaged corpse, says 'Believe in everyone,' and vanishes. The shinigami arrives, but under its mask is her mother, Akane Kogori. Akane dies by police gunfire; Mifuyu Niimura goes missing.\n　A month later, Motoki-cho grown hard to live in, Natsumi and Haruka move to their parents' family homes. But Haruka, who moved to the Arata settlement, falls out of contact. Two years later, Natsumi and Erina head there to find her.

Erina Goto believes Chigaya Niimura is the ringleader of the curse-killings and presses her. Chigaya does not deny it, and intimidates Erina into stepping no further. But Chigaya's single remark, "I wanted to kill Mom too," makes Erina realize that her deduction was entirely wrong.\n　Meanwhile, Haruka Niimura, regretting that people have left the Arata settlement and that the settlement itself is in danger of dying out, resolves to protect it herself and says goodbye to Natsumi Kogori and the others. But just then, she hears the voice of the late Erika Niimura, asking her to protect the Arata settlement from afar.

Erina Goto surmises that the Megasawa City murders were an alibi contrivance using the rites for Eiichiro Niimura and the Kogori couple, and that Mifuyu Niimura, the principal offender, used a bug and the GPS function planted in Haruka Niimura's smartphone to bring the harm to Natsumi Kogori and the others as well. Haruka Niimura turns this around, lures Mifuyu Niimura to her home, and succeeds in arresting her while disguised as Eiichiro Niimura's mother. How the vanishing-trick crimes of the Megasawa City murders were made possible remains unknown, but that should come out in the questioning ahead.\n　Natsumi Kogori and Haruka Niimura, who have both lost their parents, come to live together in the Niimura house, and on that first night something impossible spreads out before the two of them.
